01 / ORIENTATION

Choose for the workload and its invariants.

This library preserves all 643 entries from the supplied research pack dated 23 September 2026. It includes engines, embedded databases, warehouses, search and vector systems, managed services and developer platforms. They operate at different architectural layers and are not interchangeable.

A popularity score is not a correctness guarantee.

Stack Overflow reported use and DB-Engines popularity measure different things. Imported numerical snapshots have not all been independently revalidated. A catalogue listing does not establish current maintenance, suitability or deployment share.

02 / ENGINEERING FOUNDATIONS

Understand what the database promises.

Relational, document, key-value and wide-column models

Relational systems model records and relationships through tables, keys and constraints. Document systems group related values into documents. Key-value stores organize access around keys. Wide-column systems commonly use partition and clustering keys for distributed access patterns. Features overlap, so evaluate the actual engine rather than relying only on the category.

Graph, time-series, search and vector systems

Graph queries emphasize relationships and traversal. Time-series workloads emphasize timestamped observations and retention. Search systems build indexes for retrieval and relevance. Vector systems retrieve by similarity in an embedding space. These may be standalone databases or capabilities added to another engine; decide where authoritative data lives and how derived indexes are rebuilt.

OLTP, analytics and embedded deployment

Transactional workloads often involve many small reads and writes with concurrency requirements. Analytical workloads often scan and aggregate larger datasets. Embedded databases run in the application's process; client/server databases expose a service boundary. Warehouses and lakehouse platforms introduce additional storage, compute and governance choices.

Transactions, isolation and consistency

Atomicity groups changes into an all-or-nothing unit. Constraints protect valid states. Isolation describes interactions between concurrent transactions; durability concerns acknowledged changes surviving failures under stated assumptions. Distributed read consistency is a related but separate question. Define the anomalies your application can tolerate and test the database's documented behavior.

Indexes, query plans and partition keys

An index can reduce read work at the cost of storage and write maintenance. Query plans reveal execution choices; measure with representative data and parameter values. Partition keys affect data distribution and hot spots. Adding indexes or partitions without measuring the workload can increase complexity without improving latency.

Replication is not a backup strategy

A replica can repeat an accidental deletion or unwanted change. Define recovery point and recovery time objectives, retain appropriate backups, and rehearse restoration. Include credentials, migrations, encryption keys and application compatibility in recovery planning. Test degraded operation and failover, not only healthy throughput.

Secure application boundaries

Bind user-controlled values through parameterized APIs. Authorize operations before accessing protected data, give services only the permissions they need and keep database credentials outside browser code. Constraints protect data integrity; they do not replace application authorization. CODARIS accesses PostgreSQL through libpq from the native C backend.

A practical evaluation checklist
  1. Write down entities, relationships and durable invariants.
  2. List real queries, write rates, contention and retention requirements.
  3. Prototype transactions and failure scenarios with representative data.
  4. Measure query plans, resource use and operational costs.
  5. Verify restoration, migration and upgrade procedures before committing.

03 / TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDES

Roles, mechanics and tradeoffs.

Twelve editorial starting points with primary documentation links. Typical users describe engineering roles, not measured demographic shares. Remaining catalogue entries retain their original data and source notes.

PostgreSQLRelational database / server

Role & typical users

Backend engineers and database developers use PostgreSQL for structured application data, queries and durable invariants.

Technical model

Tables, SQL, foreign keys and transactions model related records. Indexes support access paths; concurrency and transaction isolation govern how concurrent work observes changes.

Engineering considerations

Use constraints for durable rules, parameterized queries for values and explicit transaction boundaries. Inspect query plans and test backup restoration. CODARIS uses PostgreSQL through libpq from its native C backend.

Try building

Build a reading-list schema with unique and foreign-key constraints, then test a concurrent update.

Primary documentation ↗

SQLiteEmbedded relational database

Role & typical users

Application and device developers use SQLite when data should live with the application rather than behind a separate database server.

Technical model

An in-process SQL engine stores a database in a local file. Transactions and indexes remain useful even when there is no separate server process.

Engineering considerations

Plan file ownership, backup and write contention. Embedded deployment changes operational boundaries; it does not make concurrent writes unlimited.

Try building

Build an offline catalogue and verify a rollback leaves no partial update.

Primary documentation ↗

MySQLRelational database / server

Role & typical users

Backend and database teams use MySQL for SQL-based application storage and transactional workloads.

Technical model

The InnoDB storage engine provides transactions, row-level locking and foreign keys. SQL queries use indexes and an optimizer to select access paths.

Engineering considerations

Review isolation, deadlocks and index choices. Treat migration locking and replication behavior as operational design decisions.

Try building

Model an order and its items with a transaction and test rollback on failure.

Primary documentation ↗

MongoDBDocument database

Role & typical users

Application developers use MongoDB for data represented as documents with related values and nested structures.

Technical model

Documents can embed related data or reference other documents. Schema design follows access patterns; indexes support queries and validation can constrain stored shapes.

Engineering considerations

Flexible schema still needs a data model. Weigh duplication and document growth against the cost of separate reads and cross-document updates.

Try building

Model a product catalogue and compare embedding variants with referencing them.

Primary documentation ↗

RedisIn-memory data store

Role & typical users

Backend and platform engineers use Redis for fast access to keys and data structures in workloads such as caching and coordination.

Technical model

Strings, hashes, lists, sets and other structures expose purpose-specific operations. Persistence, eviction and replication settings shape operational behavior.

Engineering considerations

Decide whether data is authoritative or rebuildable. Define expiration, eviction and cache-miss behavior; do not assume every deployment has the same durability guarantees.

Try building

Build a bounded cache and test expiry, eviction and upstream failure.

Primary documentation ↗

Apache CassandraDistributed wide-column database

Role & typical users

Distributed-systems teams use Cassandra for partitioned data and workloads designed around known access patterns.

Technical model

Partition keys distribute records; clustering organizes data within partitions. Replication and tunable consistency affect availability and read/write behavior.

Engineering considerations

Design queries before tables and avoid unbounded hot partitions. Plan repairs, retention and failure testing rather than treating distribution as automatic reliability.

Try building

Design a time-bucketed event table and explain its partition-size bound.

Primary documentation ↗

Neo4jProperty graph database

Role & typical users

Developers working with connected data use Neo4j to model relationships explicitly and traverse them.

Technical model

Nodes and relationships can carry properties; labels and relationship types express meaning. Graph queries follow patterns across connected records.

Engineering considerations

Bound traversal depth and inspect query plans. Graph modelling is useful when relationships drive the queries; it does not remove indexing or transaction design.

Try building

Model projects, contributors and dependencies, then query a bounded dependency path.

Primary documentation ↗

ElasticsearchSearch and analytics system

Role & typical users

Search and platform teams use Elasticsearch to retrieve and aggregate indexed documents.

Technical model

Search visibility is near-real-time: an indexed change may require a refresh before appearing in search results. Analysis and mappings influence how text is indexed.

Engineering considerations

Design reindexing and source-of-truth recovery. Distinguish acknowledgement from search visibility and budget shard count, memory and storage.

Try building

Index a small document set and test the interval between a write and searchable results.

Primary documentation ↗

DuckDBEmbedded analytical database

Role & typical users

Analysts and data-tool developers use DuckDB for SQL analytics within an application or local workflow.

Technical model

An in-process analytical engine supports column-oriented execution and data-file workflows. Its role differs from a shared transactional application server.

Engineering considerations

Test memory requirements and representative scans. Separate analytical access patterns from highly concurrent request-by-request updates.

Try building

Query a local dataset and compare a full scan with a filtered aggregation.

Primary documentation ↗

Amazon DynamoDBManaged key-value and document database

Role & typical users

Cloud application teams use DynamoDB for managed, partitioned application data with key-oriented access.

Technical model

Partition and sort keys shape access patterns. Secondary indexes add alternate query paths; throughput and consistency behavior depend on the operation and configuration.

Engineering considerations

Avoid hot keys, understand index limitations and model cost under real traffic. Managed operation still requires access control, backup and failure planning.

Try building

Design keys for a tenant-scoped activity feed and test a heavily active tenant.

Primary documentation ↗

QdrantVector search system

Role & typical users

Search and machine-learning teams use Qdrant to retrieve vectors by similarity with associated payload filters.

Technical model

Collections organize points containing vectors and payload data. Similarity search depends on the embedding model, distance metric and index configuration.

Engineering considerations

Measure recall and latency on representative queries. Enforce tenant filters and plan embedding-version migrations; similarity is not factual correctness.

Try building

Create a small semantic-search benchmark with labelled relevant results.

Primary documentation ↗

SupabaseDeveloper platform / PostgreSQL foundation

Role & typical users

Application teams use Supabase to combine a PostgreSQL database with platform services and developer-facing APIs.

Technical model

The database remains PostgreSQL, while the platform supplies additional integration surfaces. Engine capabilities and platform responsibilities are distinct layers.

Engineering considerations

Design row-level access policies and keep privileged credentials on the server. Review backups, migrations and the trust boundary of every exposed API.

Try building

Create a tenant-owned table and test policies with two different users.

Primary documentation ↗

06 / LAYERS & RESPONSIBILITIES

An engine is not the whole platform.

A managed service runs or packages database capabilities. A developer platform may also expose authentication, APIs, storage or realtime features. Compare the underlying data model and guarantees separately from hosting and application services.

The 24 source-pack profiles below retain their dated notes. Product offerings can change; check each linked provider before making a deployment decision. MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas, for example, represent an engine and a managed platform rather than two interchangeable data models.

08 / COVERAGE & LIMITATIONS

Read the methodology.

This broad catalogue is not an exhaustive list of every database ever built. Source labels are preserved even when broad or combined; the technical guides provide additional context for their covered products.

Workbook overview

CODARIS Databases & Data Platforms Research Dataset

Metric · Value

CODARIS catalogue entries · 643

DB-Engines DBMS in Sep 2026 ranking · 438

Stack Overflow 2025 database respondents · 26083

Stack Overflow usage rows captured · 16

DB-Engines top systems captured · 20

Primary model/category labels · 36

Research sources · 21

IMPORTANT TAXONOMY: MongoDB and PostgreSQL are database engines/DBMS products; MongoDB Atlas and Neon are managed services/platforms; Firebase is a developer platform whose database products include Firestore and Realtime Database; Supabase is a development platform built around PostgreSQL. CODARIS should keep these distinctions visible rather than labelling everything simply 'database'.

POPULARITY METRICS: Stack Overflow measures self-reported developer usage. DB-Engines is a monthly popularity index using multiple signals. Neither is a census or literal market share. Do not average these columns into one universal score.

Methodology
Methodology
IssueCODARIS treatmentWhy
What counts as a database?Catalogue database engines, managed database services, warehouses, embedded databases, search/vector data systems and developer data platforms, but preserve Product Type and Primary Model.Developers commonly choose among all of these, but they are architecturally different layers.
DB-Engines rankingShow rank and score only as DB-Engines popularity index values, dated September 2026.The score is generated from several popularity signals and is not a percentage of developers or deployments.
Stack Overflow usageShow 2025 'Have Used' percentage only for environments with verified published values.The database question had 26,083 respondents and allowed multiple selections.
FirebaseTreat Firebase as a developer platform; list Cloud Firestore and Firebase Realtime Database as the actual database products.Avoids presenting a platform brand and its databases as if they were one engine.
Supabase / Neon / PlanetScaleClassify as managed developer/database platforms and retain their PostgreSQL, Vitess/MySQL or other foundations.Users need to understand whether they are selecting a database engine or an operational platform around one.
Search and vector systemsInclude systems such as Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant and Weaviate, labelled by type.Modern application data architectures increasingly use search/vector stores alongside transactional databases.
Country dataDo not infer per-database country shares from overall respondent geography.A country's representation in a survey does not establish database usage in that country.
Gender dataLeave per-database gender values blank unless an explicit cross-tab with sample sizes is available.Prevents fabricated demographic precision and preserves non-binary/non-response categories.
CompletenessCall this an extensive curated catalogue of 643 entries, not 'every database ever made'.DB-Engines alone tracks 438 DBMS products, while platforms/services create additional naming and taxonomy complexity.

09 / PROVENANCE

Follow the evidence.

All 21 source records are retained. Original JSON, CSVs, workbook and README are preserved in the repository. Imported numerical values are attributed snapshots, not live counters. Source licensing and attribution remain applicable; linked documentation is not reproduced in full.
